lower_layer_finding.investigation_priority: A typed primitive-fraction entry at the scalar owner could eliminate the impossible denominator-error transport and support the whole unsigned range directly. findings: Rational primitive conversions already use separate signed/unsigned From implementations; no typed fraction conversion was found.

from_fraction_parts_reduced is private in rational::arithmetic. A typed fraction conversion can live beside construction or use a narrowly visible helper; do not duplicate its zero, dyadic, GCD and trace sequence.

Current Interface uncertainty arrives as signed i64/u64 config Rational. The unsigned interval constructor was only a rejected prototype. A proposed full-u64 direct conversion must not claim identical dispatch to that prototype's high-u64 division fallback.
Keep existing fallible fraction and malformed denominator behavior. At the domain boundary a NonZeroU64 must come from validated data or explicit checked construction, never an unchecked assumption.

The absence of a typed ingress is a candidate ownership improvement, not a correctness bug or evidence that the compiler currently pays for an impossible error. That cost still needs an isolated before/after consumer measurement.
further_read_only_review.next_missing_witness: For signed primitive typed ingress compare exact canonical numerator/denominator, display/serialization and complete dispatch against existing fraction across zero, i64::MIN/MAX, powers of two, common factors, coprime and maximal denominator inputs. For unsigned new domain use independent BigInt/BigUint expectations; do not impose a false historical trace identity. findings: Configuration Rational exposes signed i64 numerator and u64 denominator; validation rejects zero denominator, noncanonical zero and nonreduced fractions.
Scalar validation rejects negative uncertainty; wire decoding rejects uncertainty numerators that do not fit i64. Thus admitted Interface uncertainty lies in 0..=i64::MAX.

The rejected nonempty prototype checked NonZeroU64 and u64::try_from at ingress, then still transported a Result from the interval factory. Its above-i64 division fallback was unreachable for validated Interface facts, although it advertised a general u64 constructor.
configuration_domain_review.narrowest_next_experiment: Test only a typed unsigned primitive fraction ingress needed by the interval radius factory, reusing the existing fraction reducer. A signed typed fraction overload and rewriting the existing fallible fraction are not prerequisites; avoid extra public API and unrelated codegen changes. Preserve malformed-input errors at ingress.
witness_partition: For 0..=i64::MAX, require identical exact canonical values and full numeric dispatch to Rational::fraction(n as i64,d). Include zero, powers of two, common factors, coprime pairs, maximal denominators and boundary values.

For larger u64 numerators, verify exact canonical values against an independent arbitrary-integer oracle and defining quotient identities. Do not claim trace equality to the rejected division-based prototype.
Do not skip fraction reduction merely because configuration currently validates canonicality. That would require separate transported proof and would change the governing dispatch contract.

A migration that converts the integer separately for nominal and endpoints would add scalar-construction work and must not claim identical dispatch. Preserve single conversion and order when designing shared arithmetic.
